title: Maximum K to Sort a Permutation
summary: Given an integer array nums of length n, which is a permutation of the numbers in the range [0..n-1], you can swap elements at indices i and j if the bitwise AND of nums[i] and nums[j] equals a non-negative integer k.
statement: Given an integer array nums of length n, which is a permutation of the numbers in the range [0..n-1], you can swap elements at indices i and j if the bitwise AND of nums[i] and nums[j] equals a non-negative integer k. Determine the maximum value of k that allows the array to be sorted in non-decreasing order through any number of such swaps. If the array is already sorted, return 0.
constraints: nums is a permutation of zero through n-1.
You may swap two values only when their bitwise AND equals the chosen k.
Return the largest k that permits sorting, or zero if already sorted.
hints: Only values outside their final positions need to participate in swaps.
The maximum feasible k is the bitwise AND of every misplaced value.
Initialize with all bits set, AND each value whose index differs, then map the sorted sentinel to zero.
Every required participant must contain every bit of k, while their shared AND is itself achievable and is the largest such mask.
editorial: Every required participant must contain every bit of k, while their shared AND is itself achievable and is the largest such mask.

tests.explanation: Only three and one are misplaced; their AND is one.
The misplaced values three and two have AND two.
